terminologyReview: Guideline clarification: the revised distinction in references/common.md and references/ga.md is correct. The evidence agrees on three points. intl-workerd.json shows Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat unsupported (English output) for eo, be and ga, while Intl.PluralRules returns native categories for all 18 locales. InstructionTemplates (packages/shared/src/instruction-template.ts) builds Intl.PluralRules for the content language and throws when a catalog omits a native count variant or a message. BotText.andList and transcriptLabelList join items only through the catalog's formatting.* patterns. So Bickr's own formatters never 'silently return English'; the English fallback is only a property of the platform Intl list and relative-time formatters, which Bickr does not use for these strings. One leftover: references/eo.md line 7 still says 'The runtime formatters silently return English, although plural rules work.' It should use the same wording as common.md and ga.md (be.md already does). This is a guideline edit only and changes no frozen English unit.

Arabic terminology: الاستمرار now means continue in all three continue units, and متابعة/المتابعة remains only for following a participant (system.main, follow and unfollow units, reminder activity lists). Tool descriptions open with third-person descriptive verbs. سأقرؤه is used consistently, and every recovery.unknown.* unit uses the vowelled active لم يُعِد. The capacity units use يمكن ... ما لا يزيد على, and the four true "must be at most" or "no more than" units (structured_output.maximum.*, textTooLong) keep يجب ألا يزيد, which matches the source force.

Neutral counts versus numeric duals: the neutral constructions are grammatical for zero, one, two, few, many and other, and they preserve the elapsed or remaining quantity and its direction. Numeric fragments with digits work for one, few, many and other, but the two category (n = 2 only) forces either a digit plus a dual noun (a doubled number) or a dual noun without the visible count, which common.md forbids. Neutral wording is therefore the correct requirement-level choice. My optional alternative for the ten time.* units keeps neutrality while restoring the compact قبل/بعد fragment.
uncertainties: Unresolved style question for the lead: should the time.* JSON "when" values stay full sentences ("المدة المنقضية بالساعات هي N.") or use the compact count-neutral fragment ("قبل مدة عدد ساعاتها N")? Both are grammatical in every category; neither changes the fact. A native Arabic reviewer should confirm which reads more naturally in a tool result.

The lead record notes a detached و before opaque values (for example "lang و text") as an intentional formatting compromise that preserves token bytes. I agree it is correct for protected tokens; it is a typographic deviation, not a grammar error.

(1) eo.md and be.md now say what common.md and ga.md say: in Workers, Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English for these languages, Intl.PluralRules supports them, and Bickr uses explicit catalog patterns and rejects missing entries. (2) fr.md, pt.md and it.md now say that count parameters render ASCII digits, that a category does not insert million/milliard, milhão/milhões or milione/milioni, that de/di follows only the written numeral construction, and that many may match other for an all-digit numeral. This matches String(value) in instruction-template.ts and the platform labels "il y a 1 000 000 minutes", "há 1.000.000 minutos" and "1.000.000 minuti fa". (3) de.md separates positive obligations (Sie müssen) from prohibitions (dürfen nicht), states that "Darf nicht leer sein" is the form for a required nonempty value, and warns that "muss nicht" means need not. That is the correct German modal system: English "must not" maps to "darf nicht", not to "muss nicht".

Arabic: all ten time.* units now use the same compact count-neutral قبل/بعد fragment, and no sentence or period remains in a relative-time field. Guillemets are used around inserted titles, and tanwin is written on the preceding letter throughout.
uncertainties: A native Arabic reader can still judge whether "قبل مدة عدد ساعاتها N" reads naturally in a tool-result field. It is grammatical in every category and states the same interval, so this is a fluency question, not a correctness question.
